boldine, at concentrations that fully prevent lipid peroxidation, does not protect hepatocytes against TBOOH, but rather that boldine, by virtue of its potent antioxidant properties, prevents lipid peroxidation which, in turn, is responsible for the hepatocellular damage caused by the peroxide.
boldine, at a concentration that fully inhibits TBOOH-induced lipid peroxidation, is unable to prevent the peroxidative and lytic damage to isolated hepatocyte induced by the peroxide.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cytoprotective effect of boldine against the TBOOH-induced damage to hepatocytes was not related to its antioxidant property but rather to the ability of the alkaloid to prevent the peroxidative damage.

the protective effect of boldine against peroxidation and cell death induced by TBOHOH in isolated rat hepatocytes is due to its antioxidant properties, and that the cytoprotective effect of boldine is not mediated by a scavenger mechanism.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoprotective action of boldine against TBOOH-induced hepatocyte damage is not due to its antioxidant properties, since the latter were not required to afford the cytoprotection.
the cytoprotective action of boldine against TBOOH-induced damage to rat hepatocytes is not mediated by a direct antioxidant mechanism.
, while boldine exhibits a potent antioxidant activity, this does not necessarily translate into an effective cytoprotection of the hepatocytes against the oxidative damage caused by peroxides.
